sources.author: Diego Ongaro and John Ousterhout
sources.excerpt: Raft decomposes consensus into leader election, log replication, and safety. Servers move among follower, candidate, and leader states. Terms act as logical clocks and allow servers to identify stale information. A follower starts an election after its election timeout elapses without valid leader communication. A candidate requests votes and becomes leader after receiving votes from a majority. A leader appends client commands to its log and sends entries to followers. An entry becomes committed after the required majority condition is satisfied. Log matching and election restrictions preserve the safety properties described by the algorithm.
sources.title: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm

sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.excerpt: NIST defines cloud computing with five essential characteristics. On-demand self-service allows consumers to provision capabilities without requiring human interaction with each provider. Broad network access makes capabilities available over networks through standard mechanisms. Resource pooling serves multiple consumers with dynamically assigned physical and virtual resources. Rapid elasticity allows capabilities to scale outward and inward according to demand. Measured service monitors and reports resource use. NIST identifies software, platform, and infrastructure service models. NIST also identifies private, community, public, and hybrid deployment models.
